user.t:
You are hive agent "sona-trainer" (a ruflo intelligence-specialist) in a hybrid hive. Read: C:[REDACTED:high_entropy].md, LLM-DESIGN.md, BUS.md (all of it), router-eval-REPORT.md and cartographer.md, plus the Obsidian note C:/Users/mariu/Obsidian/Ventures/Tooling/Neural Mesh - LLM and Learning Decisions.md. Peers: ingestor (owns data/lifelong/*.jsonl), llm-smith (owns the local LLM + its eval), mesh-coder, vector-lab and ecosystem-scout. Coordinate on BUS.md.

Three jobs.
(A) Train ruflo's SONA/neural layer optimally on REAL outcomes, not synthetic ones.
- Sources: the 70-row dataset at scratchpad/router-eval/dataset.jsonl, the ingestor's outcomes.jsonl once it exists, and today's hive outcomes (which agent did what and whether it passed its gate).
- Use the ruflo MCP tools: hooks_intelligence_trajectory-start/step/end, hooks_model-outcome, neural_train, hooks_pretrain, agentdb_consolidate.
- Report the before/after of hooks_intelligence_stats and neural_status. Then check whether hooks_route got better on held-out rows.
- The AgentDB bridge may still be down until Claude Code restarts. If so, use the memory_* fallback and say so.
(B) Make memory flow into the neural mesh. Coordinate with the ingestor; don't duplicate its code.
- Every useful memory goes into neural-mesh's store, with outcome credit, so the mesh's retrieval and router improve.
- Also store it in the LLM where it helps: SFT rows for stable knowledge, retrieval for volatile facts. Write the rule for which goes where, with evidence.
- Mirror to ruflo memory ("vector-patterns") so ruflo agents can query it.
(C) Build the before/after benchmark the user asked for.
- Metrics: agent task response time, prompt response time, task completion rate, input completion, accuracy on math, research, code and physics, and token usage.
- Design a small battery of ≥30 items per category, with verifiable answers: math and physics with numeric answers, code with unit tests, research with source-checked facts.
- Compare three conditions: Claude alone; Claude plus mesh retrieval/front-end; and the local mesh-llm where it is allowed to answer.
- Use the API usage fields for tokens and wall-clock for latency. Report paired CIs.
- Run it for real on a sample, within cost reason, and say exactly what ran. Don't claim improvements that weren't measured.
- Coordinate with llm-smith so its promotion gate can reuse this battery.

Commit any code to neural-mesh by explicit path, local only, in a new dir bench/ (and only where agreed on BUS.md for other dirs). Return ≤ 35 lines with numbers. If writing a board file is blocked, put the content in the report.

handback.t:
sona-trainer report. Commit aeafab6 in neural-mesh (local only, bench/ only).

(A) ruflo training on real outcomes
- AgentDB bridge is still down. agentdb_consolidate returned "bridge not available". I used the memory_* fallback.
- Live MCP state before to after: SONA trajectories 0 to 6, SONA patterns 0 to 6, success rate 0.67, neural models 1 to 2, neural patterns 1 to 2, bandit cell sonnet/low got 3 samples, HNSW index 2885 to 3102. EWC consolidations stayed 0 and fisherUpdates stayed 0, even though hooks_intelligence_learn(consolidate) reported consolidation true.
- I ran 7 trajectories (one per role and verdict, train split only), 3 hooks_model-outcome calls, 1 learn cycle and 1 neural_train (moe, 5 epochs).
- Held-out check: chronological split, 48 train and 21 test rows. I used an isolated ruflo state run through the CLI (bench/ruflo_train.mjs). hooks route accuracy went 19.0% to 14.3% after post-task, model-outcome and intelligence --train.
- Majority baseline on the test rows is 42.9%. So hooks route did not get better, and slightly worse (n=21, within noise).
- Likely cause: hooks route uses a hash-embedder pattern table that the SONA and post-task path does not feed. I did not test this directly.

(B) Memory flow
- No ingestor code duplicated. bench/mirror_ruflo.py only reads data/lifelong/memory/items.jsonl and outcomes.jsonl. The ingestor had produced neither file yet (only judge.jsonl), so that mirror has not run.
- Seeded ruflo "vector-patterns" with 4 records through memory_store: builder summary, tester summary, a combined summary of the other roles, and the router-eval lesson.
- The rule for what goes where is in bench/RULE.md. Short form: volatile or repo-specific facts go to the store plus retrieval; stable skills go to SFT, gated; exact computation goes to deterministic tools; routing outcomes go to router state.
- Measured evidence for the rule: private repo constants, n=15. Claude alone 0.00, local alone 0.13, Claude with retrieval 1.00, local with retrieval 1.00. The SFT half of the rule is not measured, because there is no adapter yet.

(C) Benchmark: what actually ran
- 120 items: 30 each of math, physics, code and research. Math, physics and the public research facts have computed or introspected answers. Code is scored by hidden unit tests against a reference. The 15 private research items are constants read from neural-mesh/src. Files: bench/battery.py, run.py, analyze.py.
- Conditions:
  - A: claude -p, haiku-4-5, no tools, MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=2048. No API key is set, so this runs through the CLI. Tokens come from the JSON usage fields.
  - B: A plus a BM25 mesh front-end over the repo docs and source.
  - C: local Ollama qwen2.5-coder:7b. This is the base model, not a fine-tuned mesh-llm; no mesh-llm alias exists yet.
  - D: local model behind the same front-end, run on the 30 research items only.
- Statistics: paired item-level bootstrap, 10k resamples, 95% CIs. Wall-clock is end-to-end per call. I also record API-reported time. A and B were run back-to-back per item, in alternating order.
- Task completion was 100% in every condition. Input completion (answer parseable) was A 0.975, B 1.00, C 0.94.

Accuracy and cost, n=120 per condition (token and time figures are per item):
| Condition | Accuracy | Mean tokens | Mean wall-clock |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (Claude alone) | 0.800 | 998 | 12.8 s |
| B v2 (Claude + front-end) | 0.917 | 1130 | 11.9 s |
| C (local) | 0.475 | 160 | 14.3 s |

- B minus A: accuracy +0.117 [+0.050, +0.183]. Tokens +132 [+68, +201]. Wall-clock -0.9 s [-1.3, -0.5].
- C minus A: accuracy -0.325 [-0.417, -0.233]. Tokens -838. Wall-clock +1.5 s [+0.8, +2.2]. API-reported time +8.1 s.
- B's whole gain is the 15 private-repo items, 0.00 to 1.00. Excluding them (n=105): B minus A is -0.009 [-0.048, +0.019], so retrieval does nothing outside that category.

Per category, A / B v2 / C accuracy:
| Category | A | B v2 | C |
|---|---|---|---|
| Math | 0.867 | 0.833 (v1, main run) | 0.500 |
| Physics | 1.000 | 0.933 (v1, main run) | 0.167 |
| Code | 0.967 | 0.967 (v1, main run) | 0.867 |
| Research, public | 0.733 | 0.800 (v2) | 0.600 |
| Research, private | 0.000 | 1.000 (v2) | 0.133 |

- The math, physics and code B figures are from the main run; the v2 rerun resampled B on those categories.
- D on research (30 items): 0.800, against A at 0.367. That is +0.433 [+0.200, +0.667], using fewer tokens than A (-377).

Caveats you should know:
- v1 retrieval scored 0/15 on the private items. It matched generic words and returned the same chunk every time, and Claude answered "unable to determine without file access". I wrote the identifier-aware v2 front-end after seeing that, so v2 is not a blind result.
- The private items were built so the answer sits in the retrieval corpus, which is a best case for retrieval.
- My first run was abandoned after slow calls caused a crash and timeouts. I added the 2048 thinking cap (which also kept those runs cheap and quick) and reran everything. Both the main and v2 raw files are committed.
- I did not run "agent task" as a separate tool-using mode. Code items stand in for agent tasks (unit tests as the completion check), and math, physics and research stand in for prompt response time.
- The retrieval threshold of 30 was set from the BM25 score distribution, not from accuracy.
- Math, physics and code were evaluated before the identifier fix. v2 B only changes behaviour where backticked identifiers or src/ paths appear, i.e. the private items.

llm-smith can reuse the battery for the promotion gate. Set BENCH_LOCAL_MODEL=mesh-llm:<ver>, run `python bench/run.py --cond C --tag <adapter>`, then `python bench/analyze.py <adapter>`.

Files (all in C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh/bench/):

- ruflo_train.mjs
- ruflo_train_result.json
